sentences.text: Murrindalaspis is distinguished by a dorsal plate featuring a large, blade-like, flattened, and recurved crest originating from the medial line. The type species, Murrindalaspis wallacei, possesses a high dorsal medial crest.
Unlike other acanthothoracids, Murrindalaspis lacks a ventral keel.
The genus Murrindalaspis was described by Long in 1984, with Murrindalaspis wallacei serving as the type species—the species a genus is based on.

There are two known species in the genus: Murrindalaspis wallacei and Murrindalaspis bairdi. Fossils of Murrindalaspis have been found in the McLarty Member of the Murrindal Limestone in eastern Victoria, Australia.
Murrindalaspis belongs to the parent group Acanthothoraci and is classified within the class Placodermi.
Murrindalaspis lived during the Early Devonian period, specifically between 410.62 and 393.47 million years ago during the Emsian stage.
